title: How Russia Is Attacking the Midterms with a Mother Jones Deepfake

reading.body:
This is an impersonation failure. A fabricated video was published under another organisation's branding, with a forged logo and invented quotes attributed to a named editor. The false claim was carried in the video itself rather than in any system that could be corrected, so the outlet had no way to prevent its identity being used.

The distribution happened on a social platform, where the post was surfaced to users by the platform's own ranking and recommendation systems before any human review. Detection came from outside researchers, not from the platform or the outlet, and removal followed a complaint and was actioned as a trademark violation rather than as disinformation. Catching this earlier would have required either the platform to verify the provenance of the video before amplification or the outlet to monitor for use of its brand, and neither check was in place.

The reporting describes a broader campaign using celebrity deepfakes and fake reports impersonating news outlets, and states that government units which once tracked this activity have been shut down. It is not established that the platform knew the post was fabricated before it was alerted, and the article's own assessment is that the operation has not yet achieved major reach.

reports.title: How Russia Is Attacking the Midterms with a Mother Jones Deepfake

summary:
A Russian disinformation network known as Storm-1679 or Matryoshka created a fake Mother Jones video claiming the Democratic National Committee paid $259 million to CNN chief Mark Thompson to promote gender transition among children. The video, falsely branded with Mother Jones' logo and featuring fabricated quotes from editor Clara Jeffery, was posted on X by an account called роман and viewed 155,000 times within a day, plus 50,000 more views on another account. The campaign also used deepfakes of celebrities like Sarah Jessica Parker and spread fake reports impersonating major news outlets.

Mother Jones complained to X after being alerted by researchers at @antibot4navalny, and X removed the post for a trademark violation. The article says the operation has not yet achieved major reach, but notes that the Trump administration has shut down government units that once tracked Russian disinformation, leaving the US less able to defend against influence efforts targeting the 2026 midterms.
